stories.title: Travel disruption and power cuts after back-to-back storms
summary: Authorities said they were dealing with flooding and fallen trees as Storm Boelo followed Storm Austen.

stories.title: Overnight winds reach 85mph as Scotland is hit by Storm Boelo
summary: Heavy rain and strong winds are affecting most of the country until 21:00 on Sunday.

stories.title: Flight disruption and thousands without electricity after Storm Boelo
summary: About 350 incidents, including fallen trees and flooding, have been reported to the Department for Infrastructure.

stories.title: Police using AI risks making discrimination worse, researchers warn
summary: AI tools learn from biased records and may deepen discrimination against minorities without oversight, researchers say.

stories.title: Three giant black holes discovered in a galaxy from the dawn of time
summary: Astronomers have discovered three actively feeding black holes inside a single galaxy more than 12.5 billion light-years away, revealing a remarkable scene from the universe’s infancy.
Two of the black holes are separated by just 620 light-years and are expected to eventually merge, while a third lurks farther away.
One weighs an astonishing 80 million suns, and another is growing faster than conventional theories predict.

stories.title: New evidence suggests spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater
summary: Millions of years after animals first conquered land, some took an extraordinary evolutionary U-turn and returned to the water.
Using machine learning and thousands of fossil measurements, Yale scientists have uncovered surprising clues about which prehistoric creatures truly became aquatic.
Their findings suggest that Spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater, while some ancient marine reptiles previously thought to be fully aquatic actually spent considerable time on land.

stories.title: 'What was in the Clyde is basically now on the shore'
summary: BBC Scotland reports from the scene at Cardross as Storm Boelo batters the country.

stories.title: Scientists discover how pancreatic cancer rewrites its DNA to escape treatment
summary: Scientists have discovered how pancreatic cancer cells continually reshape their genetic makeup to become more aggressive, spread, and evade treatment.
In laboratory experiments, blocking a key gene reversed some of these dangerous changes, revealing a potential new way to fight the deadly disease.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia.

Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.
The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

stories.title: More wet and windy weather to follow stormy weekend
summary: Following the first two named storms of the season, wet and very windy conditions are set to continue into the start of the new week.

stories.title: The penguins are noisy, the people fantastic - what it takes to be an Antarctic postmaster
summary: George Clarke from Bristol will run the post office at Port Lockroy in Antarctica from October to March.

stories.title: Seabirds and sewage among UNESCO status challenges
summary: A report marking 10 years of the Isle of Man as a UNESCO Biosphere highlights the scheme's progress.

stories.title: This mysterious mushroom makes people see hundreds of tiny humans
summary: For nearly a century, people in distant parts of the world have reported a bizarre experience after eating certain wild mushrooms: seeing dozens or even hundreds of tiny, colorful humans moving through the real world.
Now, scientists have identified a mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, responsible for these extraordinary hallucinations in China and the Philippines.

stories.title: Astronomers may have discovered the first moon beyond our Solar System
summary: Astronomers have uncovered evidence of a bizarre, potentially historic discovery: the first moon ever detected beyond our Solar System.
Unlike familiar moons, this mysterious object is at least as massive as Jupiter and orbits a brown dwarf, which itself circles a star.
The unusual arrangement challenges traditional definitions of planets and moons, leaving scientists unsure what to call it.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden flaw that challenges 40 years of superconductor science
summary: A superconducting material studied for 40 years has turned out to be far more complex than scientists believed.
Advanced 3D imaging revealed a hidden patchwork of crystal structures, with unusually wide boundaries that may weaken superconductivity.
The discovery challenges decades of scientific assumptions and could explain why some superconductors outperform others.

stories.title: Amber weather warning as Storm Boelo hits Scotland
summary: The Met Office has issued an amber warning for wind over Scotland from 21:00 until 21:00 on Sunday.

stories.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
summary: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure.
In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated.
Although it did not significantly outperform a placebo overall, patients with more severe hypertension showed promising reductions in blood pressure.

stories.title: A hidden bias in human language challenges 70 years of science
summary: A groundbreaking study challenges 70 years of assumptions about how human language works.
By analyzing billions of word uses, scientists discovered that meaning is organized around power, danger, and order rather than emotion alone.
Even more surprisingly, human language shows a powerful hidden preference for safety, suggesting that our words may reflect ancient survival instincts.

stories.title: NASA’s asteroid Bennu samples reveal a 4.5-billion-year-old secret
summary: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are rewriting scientists' understanding of how our Solar System formed.
New evidence suggests that Bennu was born where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.

stories.title: Scientists propose a way to detect dangerous “mirror life” before it exists
summary: Scientists have proposed a way to detect “mirror life,” a hypothetical form of life that could pose serious risks to humans, animals, and ecosystems if artificially created.
Using special fluorescent molecules and a type of polarized light also used in 3D movie technology, researchers believe they could distinguish ordinary organisms from their mirror-image counterparts.

stories.title: Astronomers uncover a mysterious magnetic web above the Sun
summary: The Sun’s seemingly peaceful regions are hiding a surprisingly complex magnetic world.

Using a balloon-borne telescope high above Earth, scientists discovered delicate, thread-like magnetic structures woven through the solar atmosphere, apparently shaped by twisting motions on the Sun’s surface.
They also mapped magnetic fields inside towering jets of solar material, revealing how those fields change with height.

stories.title: These tiny snakes roll four times faster than they slither
summary: Tiny snakes in Southeast Asia have mastered an extraordinary escape technique: rolling across the ground at speeds up to four times faster than ordinary slithering.
Scientists discovered that dwarf reedsnakes accomplish this feat through precisely coordinated body movements that allow their bodies to rotate while their heads remain remarkably stable.

stories.title: Storm Boelo to bring severe gales and heavy rain into Sunday
summary: An amber weather warning has been issued for much of Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and northern England, as Storm Boelo approaches.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden switch that burns fat and blocks new fat cells
summary: Scientists have discovered that switching off a protein called Mitch makes human cells burn more fat and prevents new fat cells from developing.
The breakthrough builds on experiments in mice that showed remarkable resistance to obesity and improved muscular endurance, raising hopes for a new approach to weight-loss treatment.

stories.title: Wales plans to ban steel pylons as government launches consultation
summary: The Welsh government says it is consulting on an "undergrounding-first approach" to electricity lines.

stories.title: Weather warnings in place ahead of Storm Boelo
summary: The amber Met Office alert for counties Antrim and Londonderry lasts from 21:00 BST on Saturday until 21:00 GMT on Sunday.

stories.title: Project to restore rare native trees with DNA testing
summary: Conservation groups say black poplars are endangered due to felling, land drainage and habitat loss.

stories.title: Historic swimming pond to be restored
summary: Specialists are looking at how to clear the Cornwall bath house pond and understand the tidal inlet.

stories.title: The people on standby when a storm strikes
summary: While most people are preparing to stay indoors as another storm approaches, others are getting ready to head straight into it.
